text:
The tone of the email is polite and professional, but it is somewhat abrupt and lacks specific details that would help the professor understand the situation and grant the request. It states the problem but does not propose a solution or a new deadline, which can make the request feel like a demand rather than a negotiation. To improve the sentiment, the email should be more respectful, provide a brief (but not overly detailed) explanation, propose a specific new deadline, and express gratitude for the professor's consideration.

Here is a revised version:

Subject: Request for Extension on Term Paper - [Your Name]

Dear Professor Smith,

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to respectfully request a short extension on the deadline for my term paper, which is currently due on [Original Date].

Due to unforeseen personal circumstances that have arisen recently, I have been unable to dedicate the necessary time to complete the paper to the standard I aim for. I understand the importance of adhering to deadlines and apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.

Would it be possible to submit the paper by [Proposed New Date]? I am confident that this additional time will allow me to produce a higher quality assignment.

Thank you very much for your time and consideration. I look forward to your response.

Sincerely,

[Your Name]
[Your Student ID]

***

The country famous for the Great Barrier Reef is Australia.
